stop_status: NO_STOP_DEFECT REMAINING IN THE REVIEWED SCOPE. The batch was INDEPENDENTLY REJECTED ON ITS FIRST CLAIM and then corrected and accepted. The rejected claim (authority parity) was false; the accepted claim is an explicit, documented section 17 divergence.

adjudication_history.reason: The author claimed the 32-bit product refusal restored authority parity. The reviewer proved the authority guard at argon2.c:732 is dead on x86-64 (sizeof yields size_t, promoting the uint32_t operand), demonstrated empirically that m_cost 0x3FFFFF/0x400000/0x400001 all reach OPENSSL_secure_calloc, and showed that our guard therefore refuses a STRICTLY LARGER input set, silently, under a false parity claim.
adjudication_history.disposition: Claim withdrawn. The fix was retained but reclassified as a deliberate divergence, and the refusal was made to raise the same error state as the allocation-failure path.

adjudication_history.reason: The refusal is correctly classified, raises byte-identical error state (PROV_ARGON2_741, 'cannot allocate required memory', 0x1C8000EB), and its input set is exactly the documented cap; both cleanse fixes are sound and their probes fire.

authority.abi: No C ABI change; no #[repr(C)], exported symbol, extern "C" signature, seam constant or lint attribute changed.
authority.authority_guard: argon2.c:732 -- memory_blocks * sizeof(BLOCK) / sizeof(BLOCK) != memory_blocks. sizeof(BLOCK) is size_t, so the predicate is always false on 64-bit and the guard never fires. Verified statically and by running the pinned behaviour: all three boundary m_cost values reached allocation.

divergence.class: known vulnerability mechanism / resource exhaustion not reproduced (AGENTS.md section 17)
divergence.statement: For any Argon2 m_cost whose post-normalization block count N = floor(m_cost/(4*lanes))*4*lanes is >= 0x400000, this crate refuses before allocation with PROV_R_INVALID_MEMORY_SIZE ('cannot allocate required memory'), whereas the pinned x86-64 OpenSSL 3.6.4 authority attempts OPENSSL_(secure_)calloc(N, 1024) and proceeds if it succeeds. All other inputs are behaviour-identical.
divergence.compatibility_consequence: When the authority's allocation fails it raises the same error state, so the difference is confined to hosts that can actually satisfy >= 4 GiB. Under Linux overcommit even that is not guaranteed: calloc may succeed lazily and fail later in fill_memory_blocks.
divergence.cap: working memory capped at 0x3FFFFF blocks (4 GiB - 4 KiB)
